items.snippet: Opus 5.5’s biggest tell is the word “dependable,” which pops up 23 times more often than in human samples.

items.title: This startup wants to turn idle car inventory into rental revenue
items.snippet: When Igor Dobrianskyi looks at a car dealership lot, he doesn't see rows of cars — he sees millions of dollars just sitting there, depreciating. Come see MyMonthlyCar in the Startup Battlefield 200 at TechCrunch Disrupt, taking place October 13 to 15 in San Francisco.

items.title: Amazon releases its own Jev clone as decision models flood the web

items.title: Shopify debuts Canvas, a way to build online stores by chatting with AI

items.title: One year later, Tesla and Musk still don't have a good definition of 'abundance'

items.snippet: The startup helps developers build AI agents that work over iMessage, SMS/RCS, email, and other messaging platforms. It's a bet that consumers will increasingly use agents instead of downloading apps.

items.title: Hearing tech startup Legato launches its AI hearing glasses
items.snippet: The glasses stem from the startup’s goal of making hearing care more accessible by addressing the cost, comfort, and stigma associated with traditional hearing aids.

items.title: Audible's new features let you explore book worlds — and use AI to talk to characters
items.snippet: Audible is rolling out new features that help listeners keep track of characters, explore places and imagery mentioned in books, and even interact with characters using generative AI.

items.title: The new Kindle ditches the raised bezel in a push toward a smaller, lighter e-reader

items.title: Blender, the 3D modeling app, is launching for Android next year; iPad app still on pause
items.snippet: One of the biggest headaches facing Google’s push to make Android more of a desktop platform is the professional sector of apps and programs, but one big name is making the effort, as Blender is working to bring its app to Android. Blender is an industry-recognized suite of tools used for 3D modeling. It’s effectively the go-to option, and for good reason. Shown off at the Blender Conference 2026, Blender is making the effort to bring its app to Android. The hour-long video goes over the details of how the app works and the roadmap for releasing the port, which is targeting a release in the first half of 2027. An APK demo is already available. The port appears to be mainly focused on tablets, which is a bigger undertaking than you might think. Blender relies quite heavily on keyboard shortcuts, so bringing a fully functional experience on a touchscreen is a massive change. It appears that a stylus is a big part of the experience. This comes at an important time, not only as Android tablets continue to advance, but also as Googlebook makes its debut. The Android-based platform opens…

items.title: iPhone 18 Pro Sales Jump in China Ahead of iPhone Duo Launch
items.snippet: Sales of iPhone 18 Pro models in China were 12% higher in the three days after launching than sales of iPhone 17 Pro models were during their entire first week last year, according to Counterpoint Research . The strong start helped Apple claim the top spot in the country's smartphone market for the week of September 14 to 20, handing it a 33% share. But the news could get even better for Apple's China market prospects this month: The iPhone Duo goes on sale October 23, and Chinese consumers have a much stronger appetite for foldable devices compared to the rest of the world. items.snippet: Apple TV appears to be unavailable for some users, following a recent outage of Apple Services that began on September 30. The original outage took down the App Store, Apple Fitness+, Apple Music, and several other services, but those are all now back online. Only Apple TV is still not working for an unknown number of users. Apple's System Status page indicates an ongoing issue with Apple TV that started on September 30 at 4:43 p.m. Eastern Time. items.title: Apple and Amazon face renewed UK antitrust lawsuit
items.snippet: A UK tribunal has allowed part of a renewed antitrust lawsuit against Apple and Amazon to move forward, over allegations that the companies restricted competition for Apple and Beats products sold on Amazon. Here are the details. Back in 2023, Apple and Amazon were hit with a proposed UK class action over a 2018 agreement that allegedly restricted which third-party sellers could offer Apple and Beats products through Amazon’s marketplace, reducing competition and, as a result, driving up prices for consumers. It is worth noting that the UK was not the only market where the agreement drew scrutiny. Apple and Amazon have faced antitrust investigations and legal challenges over similar reseller restrictions in countries including Italy, Spain, Germany, and the United States. In the British lawsuit, a class representative led by consumer law academic Christine Riefa accused the companies of reducing competition and driving up prices for consumers buying Apple and Beats products in the UK. Apple is reportedly preparing a new HomePod mini and smart home display for October 13 , with another full-size HomePod expected further down the line, as it builds a new generation of home products around Siri AI. For much of 2025 and 2026, Apple’s revamped Siri was the thing holding those products back. That’s no longer the case: Siri AI has now arrived with Apple’s OS 27 updates, removing one of the biggest obstacles to launching the new hardware. items.title: Apple’s home hub isn’t what you think it is
items.snippet: Macworld Apple may be less than two weeks away from releasing an all-new product in a new device category: a smart home hub . The device is said to be the start of a big push into the smart home category , which Apple has really only dabbled with so far. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman says Apple is finally set to announce it on October 13 , after years of waiting for the new Siri AI to arrive, which will play a central role in the new device. According to the most reliable leaks and rumors, this is what we know of the device’s design and operation: It will have a square aspect ratio with rounded corners and a 6-inch (diagonal) display. items.title: When is Apple’s next event? Dates, rumors, and what to expect
items.snippet: Macworld Apple’s September event may not have been Apple’s final event of 2026 – another launch could be coming on October 13. Apple typically has four main event windows each year: a spring event, WWDC in June, the iPhone event in September , and sometimes a further event in October. The company rarely confirms dates far in advance, and there’s no guarantee it will hold an event in every window. That leaves Apple fans – and anyone considering a new Apple device – wondering when the next event will happen and what might be announced. items.snippet: Macworld It’s been just 12 days since the iPhone 18 Pro went on sale, and some customers are already complaining about their phones. items.title: New macOS malware masquerades as Zoom installer
items.snippet: Macworld Jamf Threat Labs has posted a report on new malware that attacks macOS. The malware installer presents itself as a Zoom installer that actually installs the app, but it also installs an infostealer dubbed CloudSyncD that works in the background to capture data and send it to the attacker. The installation is presented as an app icon that is dragged to the macOS Applications folder, a common method of installation. However, because the malware lacks the proper signatures, macOS’s Gatekeeper will not allow it to run. items.snippet: Macworld Apple’s AirPods lineup falls into three main families: the AirPods 5, AirPods Pro 3 and AirPods Max 2. For most buyers, the choice is between the AirPods 5 and AirPods Pro 3. items.snippet: Macworld If you’ve been saving up to get an iPhone Duo when it launches on October 23, you might need to scrounge together a few more dollars. items.title: Get ready: Apple sets iPhone Duo pre-pre-ordering date
items.snippet: Macworld Apple unveiled its late-2026 iPhones (the iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max, and Duo) at a single event earlier this month, but admitted not all of them would be released at the same time. As reported even before the event , the two Pro models went on sale on September 18, but the Duo won’t be available until October. October 23, to be exact, with pre-orders commencing on October 16. items.title: How long does Apple support iPads? iPadOS 27, security updates and repair support
items.snippet: Macworld If you own an older iPad – or are considering buying a refurbished iPad – you may be wondering how long Apple will continue to support it and whether you should update to a newer model. Apple has one of the best software support records in the industry. Many iPads receive major iPadOS updates for six to eight years, and some continue to receive security updates even after they stop getting new features. As of September 2026, iPads that can run iPadOS 27 receive Apple’s current operating system and are fully supported. items.title: Siri may know a lot more, but it’s still not smart
items.snippet: Macworld After years of complaints about its limitations and poor overall performance, Siri finally received its long-overdue AI-centric overhaul with iOS 27. The virtual assistant now has a large language model (LLM) foundation, allowing it to comprehend natural speech and discuss a wider range of topics, uniquely analyze what’s visible on your screen, surface your personal data, and perform in-app actions when prompted. But while Siri AI undoubtedly addresses many of our main issues with its knowledge, its position in iOS 27 , while technically still in beta mode but very much available to everyone, introduces a whole new set of drawbacks.
